name: New York
summary: Statutes and the Constitution: NY Senate Open Legislation (nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/{LAWID}/{section}) is constructible, returns full section text to both WebFetch and shell, and shows a per-section revision date. It carries no official-status statement, and New York has no official online code. public.law and Justia (2025 edition) are tier-2 fallbacks. Case law: the Law Reporting Bureau slip-opinion reporter (nycourts.gov/reporter, coverage from 2003) is constructible from the NY Slip Op cite. Its corrected pages carry the official [AD3d/NY3d/Misc 3d] cite and *n page markers, and monthly listing pages give docket numbers. Court of Appeals leave dispositions are published as NY Slip Op 6xxxx-8xxxx motion decisions. Gaps: the Official Reports and the official NYCRR are on govt.westlaw.com (SITE_BLOCKED), so the NYCRR falls to Cornell LII. www.nycourts.gov, law.justia.com and iapps return a Cloudflare challenge to the shell, but WebFetch works on nycourts.gov.

citation_patterns.label: Official Reports (NY Official style and Bluebook)

citation_map.notes: There are two citation styles. The NY Official Reports style (Tanbook) omits periods (40 NY3d 405; CPLR 3211 [a] [7]; 22 NYCRR 202.8-g), while Bluebook uses periods (N.Y. C.P.L.R. 3211(a)(7) (McKinney); N.Y. Gen. Oblig. Law § 5-701). The Tanbook style manual is at nycourts.gov/reporter/Styman_Menu.shtml (reported, not fetched). Slip Op number ranges observed: 0xxxx are reported appellate and Court of Appeals decisions; 3xxxx(U) are eCourts-sourced trial orders shown as PDF and 'not selected for official publication'; 5xxxx(U) are unreported decisions with a Misc 3d NNNN(A) table cite; 6xxxx-8xxxx are motion decisions, both Court of Appeals leave motions and Appellate Division motions (the latter with (U)). The court IDs come from memory and were not checked against CourtListener. CourtListener groups the four Appellate Division departments under one id, so the department appears only in the citation parenthetical. The Senate law-ID table (94 Consolidated Laws plus court acts) is in ny-laws-senate.pattern_rules. Court acts (FCT, SCP, CCA, UDA, UJCA) and WKC are listed by the Senate outside the 94-law CONSOLIDATED table; their LAWIDs here are from the Senate's court-acts listing and should be confirmed on first use (open question). Precedence: the 22 NYCRR court-rules pattern wins over the general NYCRR pattern (the latter excludes title 22).

sources.title: Motion decisions (Court of Appeals leave to appeal; Appellate Division motions) — Law Reporting Bureau
sources.publisher: New York State Law Reporting Bureau
sources.official_status_evidence: Each motion decision has its own NY Slip Op number. Court of Appeals entries are 'uncorrected and subject to revision before publication in the Official Reports' (they later appear in NY3d tables). Appellate Division motions are '(U)', 'not subject to publication in the Official Reports'.
sources.coverage: Court of Appeals civil motions from February 2003 and criminal leave applications from January 2004. Appellate Division motions: 1st Dept from January 2003, 2d from October 2003, 3d from July 2007, 4th from September 2007. Appellate Term motions: 1st from June 2005, 2d from March 2004.

access.pattern_rules: Take the number from 'YYYY NY Slip Op NNNNN' and drop any '(U)'. Verified: 2024_74436 (Court of Appeals, leave denied) and 2023_73590 (2d Dept). In the current month use https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/current/motions/{year}/{year}_{nnnnn}.shtml (verified for 2026_77266). To find a leave disposition by Court of Appeals motion number: monthly listing https://www.nycourts.gov/reporter/motindex/mots_coa_{MM}-{YYYY}.shtml (verified for 09-2024), whose rows show Title | Motion No. (e.g. 2024-363) | Slip Op No. Appellate Term 2d Dept: mots_at2_{MM}-{YYYY}.shtml (seen in search). Current month: /reporter/current/index/mots_coa_list.shtml, mots_crimleav_list.shtml, mots_ad{1-4}_list.shtml. Other lists: Appeals Dismissed /reporter/motindex/apps_dismissed.shtml and Appeals Withdrawn /reporter/motindex/apps_withdrawn.shtml.
access.navigation: To go from a case to its leave disposition, use the monthly motion index for the months after the AD decision and search rows by case title. Rows carry the Court of Appeals motion number, not the AD docket, and Court of Appeals pages do not name the decision below.

automation.notes: The year-archive pages (coa-motions-archive.shtml) show year headings with no links visible to WebFetch, so construct the mots_coa_{MM}-{YYYY} URL instead.
